method: Each listed item was read with its stem, all options, keyed answer(s), explanations and takeaway. Statuses are manually reasoned, not inferred from a schema or automated pass rule.
limitations: Independent AI editorial/clinical-reasoning screen; not external clinician validation or psychometric validation.
Pass applies only to the recorded content hash. New or changed content requires further review.
No comparison against proprietary examination items; originality judged from author provenance and item content.
Cross-bank learning-objective overlap remains provisional until all batches are available.
Source checks below support only the explicitly associated claims; other category references are general reading unless specifically verified.

items.assessment: Snapshot re-read confirmed current content and metadata. Correct concept is basal-insulin necessity during illness, but the key is the sole comprehensive safe plan among implausible questions; can be guessed without using the type1 cue.
issues: Correct concept is basal-insulin necessity during illness, but the key is the sole comprehensive safe plan among implausible questions; can be guessed without using the type1 cue.
proposedChanges: Use parallel teaching priorities: how to continue basal insulin under the sick-day plan (key); how to choose tolerated carbohydrate foods; how to adjust mealtime doses to intake; how to resume usual activity after fever. Ask which misconception about stopping basal insulin needs immediate correction and explain ketoacidosis despite poor intake.

items.assessment: Snapshot re-read confirmed current content and metadata. Erratic glucose plus repeated injection into firm painless lump discriminates lipohypertrophy correction from dose escalation or unplanned site changes; key length does not alone decide.

issues: Key is longest and uniquely safe/general; old-pen appearance is weak filler.

items.assessment: Snapshot re-read confirmed current content and metadata. Waiting until unconscious is cartoon unsafe and the compound key is the only reasonable option.
issues: Waiting until unconscious is cartoon unsafe and the compound key is the only reasonable option.
proposedChanges: Replace alternatives with plausible early errors: eat a routine snack and check at next scheduled time; rest first and check only if symptoms persist; focus on changing tomorrow dose before evaluating current symptoms. Keep immediate available glucose check and low-glucose plan, with case-specific rationale.

items.assessment: Snapshot re-read confirmed current content and metadata. Acute renal decline/dehydration before due metformin changes administration safety; unchanged prescription and food coadministration are plausible inadequate reassurances.
